name: Riverview Innovation & Technology Campus
tac: Organized group; Coalition (civil rights/env/labor); Packed hearings; Petition; Moratorium push
notes: The developer says the project is in SEQRA and site plan review before the Town Planning Board. The board held a packed public hearing in June 2026 and tabled the item until a revised site plan comes in. The Town Board then passed a 20MW+ data center moratorium in Aug 2026. Unclear: the supervisor said the project would later go to the Town Board, and no source says what that approval would be.

name: Project Freebird
notes: The site near Burlington is in unincorporated Milam County. Texas counties generally have no zoning power (per the cited Texas Tribune/KSAT piece, which does not name Milam). The only county action found is a reinvestment zone, with any abatement held until a tenant signs (Compute Atlas, a secondary source). The Army Corps found no wetlands permit was needed (E&E News). No Milam-specific source confirms the absence of zoning.

name: Nebius Data Center
tac: Organized group; Packed hearings; Petition; Legal challenge; Moratorium push; Disclosure demands
notes: The ~400-acre Bly Rd site was rezoned to business park/industrial in 2022, before the project. Data centers are a 'right of use' in I-1 zones, so there was no land-use hearing. The public hearing and vote (5-2, Mar 2 2026) were on Chapter 100 bonds and abatement. A referendum petition was rejected, Independence GUARD Alliance sued (Sunshine Law), and a court sided with the city. The tracker lists the operator as Patmos, but the source and coordinates match the Nebius campus. Patmos has a separate pending application nearby.

name: Microsoft International Drive Campus
notes: The land at 2700 International Drive (ex-Foxconn, TID No. 5) was already zoned industrial from 2017. The Plan Commission (Jan 21 2026) and Village Board (unanimous, Jan 2026) approved site plans only. Public comment was taken, with little opposition (one resident raised concerns), but it is unclear if a formal hearing was held. The tracker lists Sturtevant, but the approving body was Mount Pleasant.

name: HCI DP Land Acquisition Data Center
notes: HCI filed for a special exception ('use not provided for') in the Industrial Park district before the Zoning Hearing Board. It also filed a validity challenge claiming the ordinance unlawfully excludes data centers, covering a larger area. The resident group says both ZHB hearings were postponed indefinitely at HCI's request, so no hearing has been held. The township is weighing a Data Center Overlay (Ord. 1-2026), and Hummelstown Borough may intervene.

name: Stanton Springs Data Center
notes: On Feb 27 2018 the Newton County BOC held a public hearing (no one spoke in opposition) and approved 5-0 a 20-year development agreement with codename Morning Hornet LLC. It lets the company build 'as it sees fit' within a footprint in the JDA-owned Stanton Springs park, and is paired with a JDA land sale, bonds and a 20-yr abatement. Officials would not confirm Facebook beforehand. No separate approval was found for the current expansion. The later pushback is a neighbors' well-water lawsuit, not an approval challenge.

name: Google Dalles Data Center
notes: The city approved an administrative site plan review (Aug 4 2026) to rebuild Google's original 2006 data center at 4200 Columbia Rd. The only process was notice to owners within 100 ft, with 14 days to comment and an appeal window to Aug 17. No hearing was held and no opposition was reported.

name: Project Lincoln: OC Data Center (second version)
tac: Organized group; Petition; Packed hearings; Moratorium push
notes: WHP's second site (Sauerbeck Drive-In, Commerce Pkwy/DW Griffith Ln) is zoned industrial. The planning director classed the data center as a 'private utility', and the Board of Adjustments denied residents' appeal at a packed hearing (June 2025). Fiscal Court passed a 150-day moratorium with no carve-out (July 2025) and WHP withdrew. It is unclear whether 'private utility' is allowed by right or needed further discretionary approval, so the path is left Unknown.

name: Databank Red Oak Campus (DFW9, DFW10, DFW11, and DFW12)
notes: The ~288.8-acre Stainback Rd campus is inside Red Oak city limits (Reinvestment Zone No. 12). The only documented local actions are a county abatement hearing (Apr 30 2024) and Ordinance 26-009 (Apr 2026) allowing overhead telecom at the Loop 9/Stainback site. No source found on the original zoning path. The 2026 Red Oak rezoning fight (830 acres, P&Z 3-2 to deny, council 4-1 to approve) was Compass Datacenters, not DataBank.

name: South Valley Technology Park Data Center
notes: South Valley is part of the 2,200 acres Tract bought inside the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center (per IREI). Under TRIC's 1999 development agreement, nearly all industrial uses are pre-approved, with no planning commission or special use permit (Governing). Tract also says the land is industrially zoned with data centers pre-approved. By right is inferred from these park-wide sources, not a project-specific permit record. The tracker's source is about Tract's separate 8,590-acre purchase.

name: Mudiita Infra Data Center
notes: Mudiita Land Venture bought ~530 acres (July 2026), but current zoning does not allow data centers and no application has been filed. The developer later said he did not want to pursue a data center 'right now' and the company websites went dark. The township held a Sept 8 2026 hearing on an ordinance to allow data centers as a conditional use in M-1/M-2. A nearby Scranton Materials overlay request was denied and appealed. 'Pending' just means not filed or decided.

name: Frightland Data Center
notes: Plans for the St. Georges Bridge/Route 13 site (Parkway Gravel; engineer Verdantas) show warehouses, but letters say the zoning allows data centers. Spotlight Delaware reports data centers are permitted by right in the county's light industrial districts. The county's Mar 2026 data center ordinance does not apply to this pipeline project. The county said the use had not been clarified, and it is unknown if the 150 homes need other approvals or hearings.

name: Quantum Leap Data Center/ Fisk University
tac: Organized group; Petition; Packed hearings; Moratorium push; Media/national attention
notes: Fisk said (June 2026) it would wait for Metro Council's data center rules before making concrete plans, and that no corporate partner was chosen. On July 21-22 2026 Metro passed zoning limits and a permit moratorium to Dec 1. WPLN says the Fisk project received permits before the rules took effect, which conflicts with Fisk's statement. The approval path is unconfirmed.

name: Project Leo
notes: The county's 2025 land use plan designated the 145th St area industrial. AVAIO's application treats the data center as warehouse/office, so no conditional use permit is needed, and it says it has earthwork permits for phase one. The Quorum Court rejected a moratorium (July 2026) and passed a data center ordinance 11-4 on Sept 24 2026 with no AVAIO carve-out. A vested-rights fight is expected. The first community meeting came in July 2026, about two years after talks began.

name: Provident Data Center/Gateway Digital Campus
tac: Organized group; Packed hearings; Moratorium push
notes: The ~575-acre Diamond Farms rezoning (agricultural to industrial) got a P&Z recommendation for approval in April 2026 after marathon, packed hearings. The County Commission approved it in Sept 2026 alongside new data center rules (1,000-ft setbacks, development agreements, escrow). The county had earlier lifted its own six-month pause. Opponents threatened lawsuits, and the end user was not disclosed.

name: Cielo Digital Infrastructure
notes: No local approval record found for a Cielo project in Clarksville/Montgomery County; trackers list only a planned 107-acre, 350MW site. As of June 2026 a Clarksville councilmember said the planning commission had received no formal data center proposal; city code requires M-2 zoning for data centers. The input source URL covers a South Carolina project, not Tennessee.

name: FO Permian Partners and HiVolt Energy Data Center
notes: A speculative 320-acre site, under option about 30 minutes southeast of downtown Midland (unincorporated county), marketed with behind-the-meter gas power; no data center builder or end user yet. Texas counties have no general zoning authority, so no local land-use approval is expected. No county abatement or other local action found. The no-zoning code is inferred from state law and the site's location.

name: CloudBurst Data Center
tac: Organized group; Legal challenge; Disclosure demands
notes: The site straddles Hays and Guadalupe counties. It left San Marcos' ETJ under SB 2038, and Texas counties cannot zone, so Hays County's only application was a flood hazard permit. On April 21, 2026, Guadalupe Commissioners Court voted 3-2 for a development agreement and a $500M tax abatement over mostly opposing public comment. In July 2026 the Data Center Action Coalition sued, alleging Open Meetings Act violations.

name: Project Mustang
notes: The Claremore Industrial Park site was reported as already zoned industrial, and no rezoning was reported. The council's vote (May 18, 2026, after packed hearings on May 5 and 18) approved a Tax Increment District and project plan allowing Beale Infrastructure 25-year ad valorem exemptions. Whether data centers are permitted by right in that district was not confirmed. Residents then sought recalls and a referendum on the TID.

name: Project Hummingbird
notes: Greene County Planning Commission minutes say Monongahela Township has no zoning, so review was under the county subdivision and land development ordinance. Conditional preliminary approval came Nov 3, 2025, and Phase 1 final approval (grading and reclamation, 910MW gas turbines, water plant) passed 8-1 on Dec 17, 2025, after public comment from about 250 attendees, most opposed. The data center end user is not identified. 'Hear' reflects public comment at the planning commission meeting, not a statutory zoning hearing.

name: Project North
notes: Project North is named only in passing, as a campus along Eynon-Jermyn Road on land sold by a local landowner. No application or approval record was found. Archbald's Nov 2025 zoning amendment requires conditional use approval for some data center projects, but other Archbald projects were reported as needing only zoning permits, so the path is unknown. The opposition, tactics and lawsuit (residents' appeal of the ordinance) are borough-wide.

name: Jailhouse Studios Data Center
notes: The approval vehicle was a 35-year county lease of the county-owned former jail to Urban Story Ventures, approved by the Hamilton County Commission on March 18, 2026. Amendments passed unanimously, including a cap of 12,000 sq ft for data storage/processing. About a dozen residents spoke, roughly half opposed, and a petition had more than 1,000 signatures. Any separate City of Chattanooga zoning review was not documented.

name: Starpointe Industrial Park Data Center
notes: Prime Data Centers is seeking conditional use approval from the Hanover Township Board of Supervisors (township governing body) for a 7-building campus plus a gas plant on about 155 acres. It falls under a data center ordinance adopted in March 2026. Hearings began in August 2026 with more scheduled through Sept 30, 2026. About three dozen residents were granted party standing, preserving appeal rights. No decision had been found.

name: QTS Kearneysville Data Center
notes: The Berkeley County Planning Commission approved a concept plan in March 2025 for the two Berkeley parcels (90-acre data center site and access parcel) of a 300-acre campus. The 191-acre Jefferson County parcel is zoned industrial, but Jefferson had received no plans. Whether any rezoning or hearing was required in Berkeley was not documented. The land was bought by IB10 Martinsburg LLC, and QTS was named in the April 2025 report.

name: Prime Storage Data Center
notes: Prime Group sought a rezoning to add data center use to its community-retail-commercial site at 1155 Powers Ferry Place. The planning commission recommended approval. The council tabled it in July 2026 and issued a six-month moratorium on other data center requests, then approved it 5-2 in August 2026. Conditions include noise mitigation and no use of city water or sewer.

name: Beacon Data Center
notes: This is the Beacon and California Resources Corp. Golden Valley Technology Hub on the Elk Hills oil field. Kern County's planning director said it would need a conditional use permit from the Board of Supervisors, and the California Energy Commission may also review it. No formal application had been filed at the time of that report. The 'No Data Centers in Kern County' coalition is petitioning against the CUP and for a moratorium.

name: Cloud Centers Data Center
notes: Cloud Centers LLC sought a special use permit and zoning variations for a 256,000 sq ft, 50MW colocation center on the former Lockformer site. The Jan 21, 2026 Planning and Zoning Commission hearing was postponed because more than 300 residents exceeded capacity. The developer withdrew in March 2026. The Village Board is assumed to be the final decision-maker; the planning and zoning commission's role is advisory.

name: LBT Investment Group LLC Data Center
notes: LBT filed a curative amendment challenge in summer 2025, arguing the zoning code was defective for not providing for data centers. Supervisors rejected it and LBT appealed to Luzerne County Court. A jointly drafted data center ordinance was tabled Feb 17, 2026, after more than 50 residents objected. No project approval had occurred, and 'Other' denotes the curative amendment/litigation path.

name: Stack Infrastructure POR03A Flagship Campus
notes: Reporting says most Hillsboro data center sites were approved via a 'Type 2' limited administrative review with minimal notice and no vote. This is generic to Hillsboro; no Stack POR03 expansion-specific land-use record was found. In July 2026 the city adopted a 120-day moratorium and hearing requirements for new projects, and a lawsuit targets enterprise zone tax-break approvals (Stack is not named).

name: Project West
notes: The developer (Project West WHP - GA LLC) requested annexation and rezoning of 513 unincorporated Troup County acres into LaGrange. In late March 2025 a motion to proceed (notify the county) died for lack of a second amid power-demand concerns, so this is a failed motion rather than a formal denial and the item could return. Troup County later adopted a 90-day data center moratorium effective Sept 16, 2025.

name: Cielo Digital Infrastructure
jur: Grundy County, IL (jurisdiction unverified; possibly Village of Minooka)
notes: Only a Cleanview listing (159 acres, planned, Cielo) was found; no local agenda, news or approval record. The tracker's source URL covers Cielo's South Carolina project, and this site is separate from the approved Equinix Minooka campus.

name: Servistar Data Center
notes: The Planning Board unanimously approved the special permit on 10/19/2021 after a joint Planning Board and City Council public hearing. The council then approved a Chapter 121A/6A tax agreement 10-3 on 10/21/2021 (three councilors opposed). The project now appears abandoned: the LLC was dissolved in 2024 and no building permit was pulled (Shoestring, Dec 2025). Only the developer, Servistar Realties, was named.

name: Midlothian 6 Data Center
jur: Johnson County, TX (jurisdiction unverified; flyer cites City of Midlothian services)
notes: The only source is a broker's sale flyer for a 3,293-acre site near Venus Switching Station. It claims 1,500 acres are zoned data center/light industrial, 1,700 acres were 'rezoned at acquisition', and a TIRZ is proposed. No government record was found to confirm the jurisdiction or any approval, and there is no named developer or end user.

name: Amazon Clinton Data Center
notes: At a 1/15/2026 special meeting, Planning & Zoning held a public hearing (no public comments) and approved a conditional use for a fence around the existing building plus a parking variance. The Board of Aldermen approved these and a FILOT the same day. The data center use itself apparently needed no approval (a CUP requirement for data centers was only added in June 2026), and Amazon was unnamed until after approval.

name: Cielo Digital Infrastructure
notes: The county's own zoning page says nothing currently restricts what happens on a sold parcel. A zoning ordinance was only being drafted in 2025-26 and would cover just the I-85 corridor. The only local vote was County Council's final approval of tax incentives on 6/23/2025 for the Hwy 329 / Broad River site (Post and Courier). The project was called Project Kingfisher before Cielo was named, and no hearing on land use was found.

name: Athens Shoals Crossing Data Center
notes: The only record found is a July 2023 administrative Plans Review notice (PR-2023-07-1387, 0 Voyles Rd / 105 Old Elberton Rd, 'New Data Center with Office Space'). No rezoning was found, but that is not confirmed, and the outcome was not verified. This appears separate from the 2025 FAE Clark rezoning that was denied (north of Winterville), though that is not certain.

name: Grindcap
notes: In June 2025 the City Council unanimously rezoned 31.4 acres at 1751 Bells Ferry Rd from Community Retail Commercial to Light Industrial, with a special use permit for relocating a cell tower. Residents raised concerns at the public hearing (Atlanta News First). A group, 'Not For Us - Cobb County', formed after approval, and the developer was named but not the end user.

name: Arnold Air Force Base Data Center
jur: U.S. Department of the Air Force (federal land), Coffee County, TN
notes: This was a federal Enhanced Use Lease solicitation on Air Force land, so there was no local zoning path. It ended in June 2026 when the Air Force said prospective developers would not submit proposals. 'Withdrawn' is approximate because no developer was ever selected. Coffee County Democrats ran a petition, and the County Commission adopted a one-year data center moratorium in June 2026.

name: Digital Realty DFW37
notes: The Digital Garland Ferris campus is zoned PD 20-17. A Detail Plan for a data center (Z 22-47, 805 Holford Rd, 18.6 ac, may amend the PD) went to a Plan Commission public hearing on 11/7/2022. It is not verified that DFW37 at 1502 Ferris Rd falls under that case, or when council approved it. The city granted Digital Realty tax incentives.

name: Misty Hollow Energy and Data Campus
notes: The article states Forward Township has no zoning ordinance. The 274-acre project (Prospect RD LLC) goes through subdivision and land development (SALDO) review: township planning commission, then Board of Supervisors, which is also amending its SALDO for industrial uses. No end user has been announced.

name: Former Remington Gun Factory Data Center
notes: As of May-Aug 2026, Turin Management had filed no land-use application, and the village called plans exploratory. The village attorney warned Turin could claim vested rights if zoning changed, and discussed a local moratorium alongside the state one. Residents spoke at board meetings, a Change.org petition topped 1,000 signatures, and residents demanded transparency.

name: Project Kestrel
notes: The 380-acre KCI-29 site (Shenandoah Computing LLC; reportedly Google-linked but unconfirmed) got Port KC conduit bond and tax exemption approval in Aug 2025. No city zoning record was found. KC allowed data centers by right until its Jan 2026 ordinance, but the parcel's district and the project's filing date are not documented. The Platte County presiding commissioner publicly opposed the tax breaks.

name: Project Redline
notes: The state IEDC approved about $42M in incentives (June 2025) for an unidentified end user, and the tracker's coordinates look like the county centroid. The IEDC could not confirm whether this is the Surge Development megasite, whose PUD rezoning was withdrawn in May 2025 after opposition led by Tuttle Orchards. No local approval record was found.

name: Stack Infrastructure POR01 and POR02
notes: Stack filed a Development Review application for POR01 hours before the council's 7/27/2026 120-day moratorium, and applications already submitted may proceed (KOIN). Development Review appears to be a staff-level Type II decision with notice but no hearing, and data centers are reportedly allowed in all industrial zones. That comes from search summaries and the DCD source, which returned 403, so it is not confirmed from a page opened.

name: West Emaus Avenue Data Center/ Quantum Group
notes: An Oct 2025 zoning officer determination found a data center permitted by right in the I-3 district at 2401 W. Emaus Ave, so only a land development plan is before the Planning Commission. The commission held a packed special meeting 7/16/2026 and gave no verdict 9/8/2026. Camelot for Children's Zoning Hearing Board appeal of the by-right determination was postponed with no new date, and the end user is not disclosed.

name: Cielo Digital Infrastructure
jur: New Lenox area, Will County, IL (deciding jurisdiction unverified)
notes: Only tracker listings (141 acres, 300 MW, planned) found; no village or county agenda, filing, or news on any local land-use approval. I could not confirm whether the site is inside the Village of New Lenox or in unincorporated Will County.

name: Digital Power Optimization
notes: DPO announced a 20 MW facility on a former mill site leased from utility CWPCo in Jan 2025 and told the city in July 2025 it would not build because it found no customers. No source describes any zoning or other local approval. Tracker coordinates sit slightly north of the city, so the jurisdiction is not fully confirmed.

name: Global Stack Data Center
jur: Santa Clara County, CA (county-owned fairgrounds; land-use authority unverified)
notes: SFist lists the Santa Clara County Fairgrounds among eight Bay Area fairgrounds considering Global Stack's edge-computing proposal, still at the presentation stage. The model depends on a public-land lease, so the veto point is coded as the land deal. No site-specific approval process, hearing, or opposition was found.

name: Edged Austin
notes: Commissioners Court approved a tax abatement for EDC Austin LLC (Edged) on a split vote on March 26, 2026, and tabled a development agreement; officials said the county has limited authority over data centers and abatements are 'the only tool'. The no-zoning code rests on Texas counties' general lack of zoning power, and the date is the abatement vote, not a land-use decision. A resident objected at the meeting.

name: Ranalli Super DC, LLC Data Center
notes: The town's Data Center Advisory Committee presentation (June 2026) says the town 'believes' a data center needs a ZBA special use permit plus Planning Board controlled-site review and SEQR; the site is described as industrially zoned, and no formal application appears to have been filed. The town adopted a 6-month moratorium (hearing May 7, 2026) after heavy April 2026 pushback, and a NY statewide moratorium also applies. Only the LLC name is public.

name: Tract Phoenix Data Center
notes: Buckeye P&Z recommended the zoning change in Feb 2024 (no community members spoke). On Aug 6, 2024 the council unanimously approved a major plan amendment replacing the residential Cipriani master plan with the Buckeye Tech Corridor, plus a development agreement reimbursing up to $50M in infrastructure. I am assuming the tracker's 'Phoenix' point (south of I-10 near Johnson Rd) is this Buckeye site; developer Tract was named but end users were not.

name: Project Mila
tac: Organized group; Packed hearings; Petition; Moratorium push; Disclosure demands
notes: The Planning Commission unanimously approved Prologis's site plan on Mar 30, 2026 in a ~10-minute meeting with no public comment; staff said the plan meets existing industrial-park zoning. The city had sold the 141 acres to Prologis in Oct 2025. The end user was undisclosed, and group W.A.T.E.R. later filed an initiative petition to cap future data centers, which does not affect this project.

name: Quantum Frederick
tac: Organized group; Petition; Legal challenge; Disclosure demands
notes: The Planning Commission unanimously approved Aligned's Type 1 site plan for Buildings 2-4 on May 20, 2025, conditioned on concrete noise walls; a 2022 ordinance made data centers by-right on LI/GI land (per GovTech). I did not find records of public testimony at this approval. The tactics listed are countywide: Sugarloaf Alliance's records lawsuit and a 21,000-signature petition against the overlay zone. Aligned earlier paused over the state diesel-generator exemption.

name: EdgeConneX AUS02
notes: A county spokesperson said county control 'lies more in permitting and abatement approvals'; campus 1 got a 10-year abatement in Dec 2024, while campuses 2/3 have only grading/excavation permits and no abatement request yet. Town halls in June 2026 and a resident-organized town hall (July 2026) are not land-use hearings. Which of the three FM 535 campuses is 'AUS02' is not confirmed.

name: Kahla Project
notes: County Judge Ryder said the county 'can't keep them from coming', meaning there is no land-use approval to deny; Commissioners Court minutes show a pending abatement for a Precinct 4 data center, 10+ residents commenting against it (Dec 22, 2025), and data-center items tabled (June 2026). The no-zoning code rests on Texas counties' general lack of zoning power.

name: TXLAAR LLC Data Center
notes: The Police Jury unanimously rezoned the 1,079-acre site north of Benton from residential to industrial on Nov 19, 2025 on TXLAAR LLC's application, via the Benton-Parish MPC. The engineer said there was 'not a tenant', and one resident spoke against. Amazon/STACK were only confirmed in Feb 2026, and the Police Jury approved the final plat after a public hearing on Mar 18, 2026.

name: American Tower Edge Data Center
notes: A small (4,000 sq ft, 1 MW) edge facility at the base of an existing ATC tower (6011 Chapel Hill Rd per spec listings) that has opened, despite the tracker's 'Proposed' status. No zoning or permit record was found; it was presumably handled administratively, but that is unverified.

name: Verrus Data Center
notes: Mill Creek Corporate Center is zoned Employment Center, where data centers are an outright permitted use (no rezoning needed). Verrus's affiliate Alderstone LLC filed a land-use application on July 31, 2026, days before the council unanimously started a moratorium on Aug 3; it stays under current code and administrative review. The city was under an NDA for over a year, the project was disclosed in July 2026, and Gov. Kotek ordered the state land sale withdrawn.

name: Comanche Circle Data Centers
notes: Hood County has no traditional zoning and regulates under Tex. Loc. Gov't Code ch. 231 subch. K. Commissioners conditionally approved the concept plan in Jan 2026, rejected a moratorium in Feb, and removed the conditions on a 3-1 vote on June 9, 2026 after the developer threatened to sue; site development plan review remains. 'Hearing' reflects dozens of residents commenting at the Commissioners Court meetings rather than a confirmed formal land-use hearing.

name: Switch Pitt Race Data Center
notes: Borough Council adopted Ordinance 245 on Sept 16, 2025, after a hearing, opening the commercial district to data centers, reportedly in anticipation of this project. Switch was not publicly confirmed until 2026; its land-development plan (filed ~Aug 2026) still needs Planning Committee review and a council vote. Opposition groups include the Big Beaver Association and the Three Rivers Motorsport Preservation Society. It is unclear whether the ordinance was a text amendment, a parcel rezoning, or both.
